item.title: California just banned Waymo from all state freeways
item.description:
California has pulled the plug on Waymo's driverless freeway rides across the entire state, citing potential safety hazards.

In a statement, the California Department of Motor Vehicles said that the ban went into effect on November 11th. The crackdown follows two recent high-profile Bay Area incidents, in which Waymo robotaxis drove into an active construction closure on US-101 near Burlingame, and a separate run-in involving California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280 in San Francisco.

In its statement, the DMV explicitly labeled Waymo's freeway operations as an "imminent hazard to public safety," noting that this isn't an isolated …

item.title: JBL’s headphones that are great for in-flight entertainment are 67 percent off
item.description:
If you’re looking to upgrade your headphones before the big wave of Black Friday deals arrives, you can buy JBL’s Tour One M3 for a new low price of $149 ($300 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and directly from JBL. The deal is so good that my colleague John Higgins, The Verge’s audio and TV reviewer, popped in on his day off to tell us just how much of a steal they are at this price.

JBL Tour One M3

Where to Buy:

  • $449.95 $149.95 at Amazon
  • $449.95 $149.95 at Best Buy
  • $449.95 $149.95 at JBL

JBL’s Tour One M3 stand out largely because they come with the Smart Tx wireless audio transmitter. Frequent fliers will likely appreciate the accessory, which plugs into a plane’s in-flight entertainment system via a 3.5mm cable, allowing you to listen to audio wirelessly. It also works with other devices that lack Bluetooth support but have a headphone jack. The small touchscreen-equipped transmitter also lets you easily adjust the headphones’ noise cancellation, EQ settings, and volume. It can be used to answer calls, too.

Fancy tricks aside, the headphones get the essentials right. According to John, they offer excellent passive noise isolation, and their active noise cancellation is good enough to block out low-frequency sounds, like airplane engines. He also praises their overall sound quality, though he notes that JBL’s default tuning slightly affects midrange clarity, something you can easily fix by adjusting the EQ. They also support high-resolution lossless audio over the included USB-C or 3.5mm cable, plus spatial audio with head tracking. JBL says they can last up to 70 hours on a single charge with noise cancellation off — enough to get you through multiple long-haul flights — while the USB-C-chargeable transmitter offers up to 18 hours of battery life.

item.title: Google’s Spark AI agent becomes ‘Tasks’ — and now it’s free
item.description:
Google is rebranding its Spark AI agent as "Tasks" and making it free to use. The feature, which is powered by Google's new Gemini 4 Hydrogen AI model, can do things like create meal plans, manage your calendar, and dig through your emails to find recurring expenses you might not need.

Users in the US will get access to a few other features, including the ability for the AI agent to call businesses to compare product pricing and check inventory, purchase items with Google Pay, and sign into accounts that support Google Password Manager. US users can also assign Gemini tasks by emailing gemini@google.com or texting it.

item.title: Meta is testing a new standalone messaging app called Direct
item.description:
Meta announced Direct, a new messaging app from Instagram that it's currently testing in Turkey and Thailand on iOS and Android. Direct is essentially Instagram's direct messaging without Instagram's other features. Meta says your Instagram chats will sync across both apps if you login with the same account. You can also sign up with an email or phone number, but Meta says if you use Direct without an Instagram account, "only your contacts can start a chat with you or add you to a group."

item.title: Amflow’s new urban e-bike series is deliciously overpowered for flat city streets
item.description:
DJI spinoff Amflow has spent the last couple of years shaking up the electric mountain bike (eMTB) market with ridiculously high-torque, lightweight models. Today, it's bringing that same overengineered energy to pavement with the UE Series, its first urban commuter line.

The series consists of two models: the UE Carbon and UE Carbon Pro. Both pack 125Nm of torque, 1,100W of peak power, and an 8x max assist ratio capable of climbing 30 percent grades - all while operating quietly under 45dBA (quieter than a household refrigerator). item.title: YouTube found a new way to inflate view counts
item.description:
YouTube's view counts will now include the number of people that it estimates are watching a video together on TV. In an update on Monday, the platform says it's bringing "co-views" to public view counts across long-form videos, Shorts, and live content to provide a more "complete picture" of how people are using its platform.

YouTube, which has become even more popular on TVs than phones, also says the change will help it align with "TV industry standards," which similarly record views by estimating the number of people watching shows. item.title: The iPhone Duo feels far more intuitive with Apple’s new face unlock
item.description:
Apple is testing adding face unlock to the iPhone Duo - not true Face ID, but something a little simpler and less secure. item.title: Inside Microsoft’s giant Outlook outage
item.description:
At 9AM last Thursday, everything seemed normal. Microsoft employees were arriving on campus, ready for a regular day of emails and meetings. But barely an hour later, one of Microsoft's worst outages in history started to unfold, leaving employees, businesses, and many governments without access to Outlook emails for nearly 24 hours.

It all started in Switzerland, according to a source familiar with the outage. Exchange Online servers that power Outlook started to fall offline. item.title: The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed
item.description:
The Justice and Commerce Departments said that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after reporting suggested an investigation had been halted last year.

"While we don't typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting," the departments said in a statement issued Monday evening.
